messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — increased 5xx rate (primarily 503) from eu-west -> gateway-prod. Pager triggered. potential customer impact: short-term request failures. monitoring: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/alerts/503-euw (auto-snapshot attached)

mira: i'm primary for the shift, taking incident. starting triage.

alex: on secondary, available to jump in. what's the initial scope?

mira: symptoms: p95 latency normal, sudden spike in 503s at the gateway layer. upstream inference nodes are returning 502/timeout intermittently. looks like a mix of connection resets + overloaded kv-cache errors in logs.

sam: i'm seeing a correlated spike in connection resets from proxy (nginx) to inference pool: `connect() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)` across ~30% of connections.

mira: runbook step 1: confirm if autoscaler recently changed capacity. i'm checking autoscaler events. ops-bot, push latest scale events.

ops-bot: autoscaler events (last 30m): scale-down triggered at 9887654200 -> removed 4 inference-replica pods; scale-up attempted at 9887654500 but pending due to quota in eu-west-1 region.

alex: aha. sounds like scale-down then scale-up failure -> transient capacity gap. that explains time-limited 503s. are we still rate-limiting incoming traffic? any fallback model?

mira: traffic routing policy is strict — no soft-fallback enabled for this customer tier. i'm temporarily enabling burst capacity policy and fallback routing to smaller-quantized model to reduce errors. doing now.

sam: please paste the commands/changes you apply so i can replicate for other regions.

mira: applied routing override: `policy-set --region eu-west --fallback-model rwd-small-quant --burst=25%` (internal CLI). verifying logs..

lee: FYI: runbook link for this pattern: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/serve-capacity-gap — follow steps 2-4 for temporary mitigation, step 6 for postmortem.

mira: verifying after override: 503s drop from 18% -> 2% over last 120s. p95 stable. continued monitoring for 10m.

alex: good mitigation. next: why did scale-up stall? need to check quota + node provisioning logs. i'll take that.

sam: i'm going to notify a small set of affected customers via status page note. suggested wording: "We saw transient request failures in eu-west; mitigation in progress, no data loss expected." should I post?

mira: yes, go ahead. include ETA: ~30m for full validation. call it "service degraded — partial request failures".

ops-bot: status update publised to status.redwood: incident 9887654321 - partial request failures in eu-west.

alex: node provisioning logs show cloud provider returned rate-limit on instance creation -> quota limit hit on account. opened ticket with cloud infra: INC-2319. attaching ticket id.

mira: action items while cloud infra responds: 1) keep fallback routing active, 2) temporarily increase burst capacity where safe, 3) throttle low-priority traffic via routing rules to preserve capacity for core customers. who takes 3?

sam: i'll draft throttle rule and apply as emergency: `route-rule set --region eu-west --priority low --rate 20r/s` applying now.

lee: adding monitoring adjust: alerting threshold increased to avoid noisy page if 503s degrade to <5% while mitigations active. keep a watch.

mira: ok, summary for handoff at 9887654600: primary = mira, secondary = alex, coverage gap: verify cloud quota resolution (alex). runbook pointer: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/serve-capacity-gap and https://redwood-internal/runbooks/egress-503. customer impact: partial request failures, mitigation applied (fallback routing + throttle). last action: status page note posted. next steps: wait for cloud infra ticket update, monitor for reoccurrence, plan rollback of throttles after stable 15m.

alex: noted. if cloud infra doesn't respond in 30m, escalate to infra lead on call (morgan) and consider moving some traffic to eu-central as temporary failover.

sam: i'll stay on watch for 30m, then handback if stable. if it flares, i'll page alex/lee.

mira: final: logging quick recovery checklist for next shift: - confirm instances provisioned and registrations to pool - remove routing override once capacity healthy - capture evals for any output differences when using rwd-small-quant - start a postmortem doc (assign to alex)

ops-bot: REMINDER: create postmortem? Use template: https://docs.redwood/templates/postmortem. Assigned: alex (owner).

mira: thanks team. handoff at 9887654980 => primary going to sam for final watch; alex remains secondary for cloud escalation. leaving notes in PagerDuty/incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

sam: taking handoff, will monitor for 30m. thumbs up. :thumbsup:

lee: leaving a few log snippets in thread for postmortem. nice mitigation, good call on fallback routing.

alex: will pick up postmortem doc and escalate if cloud doesn't respond in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident 9887654321 status: MITIGATED -> degraded -> monitoring. tags: autoscaler, quota, fallback-routing.
